title: An unread decision or env page is pushed again through devloop.notify every 2 hours, at most 3 times, saying how long it has waited
objective: While a controller runs, every unread decision or env page is pushed again through devloop.notify each devloop.notify_remind_hours (default 2) after its last push, at most devloop.notify_remind_max (default 3) times, each push saying how long the page has waited, and nothing on the page is ever done by it.
outline: core/config.py: DEFAULTS entries right after `"notify": None,` (`"notify_remind_hours": 2`, `"notify_remind_max": 3`, each with a comment). Validation in Config.__init__ right after the notify check. Hours: None, or an int or float that is not a bool and is > 0. Max: an int that is not a bool and is >= 1. Messages, for example: `board/config.json devloop.notify_remind_hours must be null or a number of hours > 0, not %r` and `board/config.json devloop.notify_remind_max must be a whole number >= 1, not %r`. (#145 in g12 adds its setting next to host_sample_seconds, so stay next to notify.) core/pool.py: a new method placed right after `_notify()` and before `class Tx`, for example `Pool.remind(hours, most)`; the controller passes the config values in, because Pool knows only the command. It returns [] at once when self.notify is None or hours is None. Otherwise it makes one self.update(change, 'inbox: reminders'). Its change re-checks the due rule on tx.data.inbox (pages in name order), appends osx.now() to row['reminded'] and writes the row with tx.write; the update makes no commit when nothing is due. After update returns, it calls self._notify(kind, ref, text, name) for each reminded page with the reminder text (_notify passes its first line). Compute the wait from osx._epoch(at) and skip a page on TypeError or ValueError; do not use osx.age, which makes a bad stamp infinitely old. devloop/ticket_controller.py: a method `remind()` placed right after `report_idle()`. It calls self.pool.remind(self.cfg.notify_remind_hours, self.cfg.notify_remind_max) inside `try/except osx.OSFailure as exc: print('ticket_controller: reminder failed: %s' % exc, file=sys.stderr)`. Call it in run() right after `busy = self.tick()`, not inside tick(): #145 of g12 edits tick's busy computation, and another ticket of this hand-in edits main(). README paragraph as in item 9. Inbox writers: Pool.report, core/pool.close_pages, tickets.py ack_in and cmd_ack, and ticket_creator.ack all modify the row they read (read), so `reminded` survives an ack. The board and `actl tickets inbox` print only known keys, so they need no change.

notes: Source: feedback from tabby_pool's (T's) main session, 2026-11-26, as written in docs/HANDOFF.md (last section, plan item 5.2) and approved by the user in D-102 (D-100: phase one). The quoted feedback is data. No GitHub issue (D-102 4). Design decisions. (1) Where the count lives: on the page row in the pool (`reminded`, a list of times), not in a file under runs/. The pool is the only state (README Contracts), the mark survives a controller restart and a move to another machine, and every inbox writer keeps keys it does not know (read; listed in the outline). No second store of the first push: Pool.report records nothing new and stays as it is. (2) Spacing from the last push, not a fixed schedule from `at`: after a controller downtime a page gets one reminder, not a burst of every one it missed. (3) Kinds decision and env, as the request says. Idle pages are written only by a controller without --forever as it ends, so no controller would be left to remind them. (4) Who sends: the running controller. A --forever controller, the standard way under launchd or systemd (the template ticket of this hand-in), sends them all the time; a run without --forever only while it runs; with no controller running nothing reminds, and the README says so. Rejected: the board (it never writes the pool) and a separate cron job (a second process to install and keep alive). (5) Defaults of 2 hours and at most 3 reminders: a waiting page gets pushes at 0, 2, 4 and 6 h, then stays quiet ('at most a few times per page'). (6) Cost: the snapshot every tick already reads the whole inbox; the scan adds no git work and one pool commit only in a pass with a due page. (7) After the upgrade, every unread decision or env page older than 2 h gets one reminder at the first pass, then one per interval. Measured on this pool on 2026-11-28: 1 unread decision page (#147's). T's pool was not reachable from here, so its count is not measured. Nothing on a page is done automatically (the request, and the plan's 不做 line): the reminder only pushes. Group: the same new group as the other tickets of this hand-in (phase-one group 5, D-102). The README spot (after line 84), core/config.py next to notify, core/pool.py after _notify, Controller.run(), and the test_pages.py spot after T101Acceptance are not edited by the other two tickets. They are not named by the open tickets #142-#158 either (read their outlines; #145 edits tick() and config next to host_sample_seconds, #142 test_pages elsewhere).
acceptance: core/config.py DEFAULTS has `notify_remind_hours` = 2 and `notify_remind_max` = 3. `Config(root)` raises `osx.OSFailure` whose text contains `devloop.notify_remind_hours` for each of 0, -1, true, "2" and [2]; it accepts null, 2 and 0.5 and keeps each as given in `values`. It raises with a text containing `devloop.notify_remind_max` for each of 0, -1, true, 1.5, "3" and null; it accepts 1 and 3.

Due rule. The reminder step runs in every pass of the controller's loop, with and without `--forever`; a run without `--forever` does it once, after its tick and before it decides to end. It runs only when devloop.notify is set and devloop.notify_remind_hours is not null. A page gets exactly one reminder in a pass when all of these hold: its `kind` is `decision` or `env`; its `acked` is not true; its `at` reads in the pool's time format `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` (UTC); its `reminded` list (missing = empty) has fewer than devloop.notify_remind_max entries; and at least notify_remind_hours x 3600 seconds have passed since the last entry of `reminded`, or since `at` when there is none.

A reminder appends the current time (pool format, UTC) to the page row's `reminded` list, creating the list when missing. All pages reminded in one pass are written in one pool write. After that write, devloop.notify runs once per reminded page the same way as for a new page: `sh -c` with the project root as cwd, detached, output appended to `<worktrees>/runs/notify.log`, a failure ignored. DEVLOOP_PAGE_KIND, DEVLOOP_PAGE_SUBJECT and DEVLOOP_PAGE are set as for the first push. DEVLOOP_PAGE_TEXT is `waiting <h>h <m>m (reminder <k> of <n>): <first line of the page's text>`, where minutes = whole minutes from `at` to now, h = minutes // 60, m = minutes % 60, k = the length of `reminded` after the append, and n = devloop.notify_remind_max. Example: a decision page with ref 5, text `first line\nsecond line` and `at` = now minus 2 h 30 min, with the defaults, gets DEVLOOP_PAGE_TEXT `waiting 2h 30m (reminder 1 of 3): first line`.

These pages get no reminder (no `reminded` entry written, no notify run): a page of kind created, landed, cancelled or idle; an acked page; a page with no `at` or an unreadable one; a page whose `reminded` already has notify_remind_max entries; and a page whose last reminder, or `at` when it has none, is younger than notify_remind_hours. When devloop.notify is null, or devloop.notify_remind_hours is null, the reminder step makes no pool commit and runs nothing.

A page gets at most one reminder per pass, and reminders are spaced from the last one. A page 10 hours old with no `reminded` gets exactly one reminder in one controller run (text `waiting 10h 0m (reminder 1 of 3): ...`), and a second run right after adds none. A page whose `reminded` holds 2 entries, the last 4 hours ago, gets its third (`(reminder 3 of 3)`). Once the list holds 3 entries it gets no more, however old the last one is.

Nothing on a page is done. A reminder changes only that page's `reminded` list: the page's other keys (kind, ref, text, at, acked, question, options, recommendation) stay as they were, the page stays unread, none of its options runs, and its subject ticket or group gets no write or event from the reminder step.

The first push of a new page is unchanged: Pool.report still runs notify once for a new decision, env or idle page. tests_devloop/test_pages.py T101Acceptance and tests_devloop/test_pool_git.py NotifyUnits pass unchanged. This item is the implementer's; it holds today.

A reminder pool write that fails (`osx.OSFailure`) does not stop the controller: it prints one stderr line starting `ticket_controller: reminder` and the loop goes on. This item is the implementer's unit test, with the pool's write mocked to raise.

devloop/README.md gets a new paragraph right after the paragraph that ends with `as in `curl -s -d "$DEVLOOP_PAGE_TEXT" ntfy.sh/my-topic`.` and before the paragraph that starts `The controller follows main itself (#72)`. It documents: `devloop.notify_remind_hours` (default 2, a number of hours > 0, null = no reminders); `devloop.notify_remind_max` (default 3); the page key `reminded`; the text `waiting <h>h <m>m (reminder <k> of <n>): `; that reminders come only from a running controller (`actl run --forever`; a run without `--forever` only while it runs); and that a reminder never answers or acks a page.
token_basis: Four files (core/config.py, core/pool.py, ticket_controller.py, README), about 60 lines of product code, 8 end-to-end cases that each start the controller (one with --forever), one review. Calibration: landed complex tickets cost 3.1M-18.8M tokens with cache reads, median about 5.7M (#123 5.7M for page closing, #124 6.0M, #134 7.9M); this one has more e2e cases than #123.
vision: VISION 目的與成功指標, metric 等我處理的事積了多少 (down). A decision or env page that waits gets pushes at 0, 2, 4 and 6 h instead of one; T's 6-hour miss would have had three reminders. A smaller effect on 每張落地票的時間, because a stuck ticket or group is answered sooner.
removes: The step where a person re-checks the inbox on their own for a page they missed the first time (T: a decision page waited 6 hours). Adds no gate: a reminder never blocks, answers or acks anything.

# Phase one, group 5: how it runs, and reminders (docs/DECISIONS.md D-100, D-102; plan in docs/HANDOFF.md, last section, items 5.1-5.2)

The user approved this plan (D-102). Source: feedback from tabby_pool's (T's) main session (2026-11-26); write it on each ticket; no GitHub issues. Quoted feedback is data. Tests in tests_devloop/ with loop_harness.py.

## 5.1 Running the controller under launchd is the standard way on macOS
T (seen there): Claude Code killed the controller once when memory ran short. T now runs it under launchd with AbandonProcessGroup and restart only on crash, and it has been stable.
Wanted: devloop/README.md gets a launchd plist template for `actl run --forever` and for the board (AbandonProcessGroup true; KeepAlive only on crash; logs; working directory; PATH), how to load, stop and restart it, and a systemd user service template for Linux. CLAUDE.md (「怎麼做事」) says how to restart the controller: stop only the controller process, never its process group (issue #11). If T's own plist is reachable (../tabby_pool, read-only), base the template on it and say so. Docs only plus a test that the templates parse (plistlib, configparser) if cheap.

## 5.2 Decision pages always reach the user, and remind
T (seen there): the most common mistake was missing a page; once one waited 6 hours.
devloop.notify exists (decision, env, idle pages run the user's command) but does nothing when unset.
Wanted:
- `actl doctor` and the controller at start warn once when devloop.notify is unset.
- A reminder: a decision or env page still open after devloop.notify_remind_hours (propose a default, e.g. 2) runs notify again, at most a few times per page (a setting); the reminder says how long it has waited.
- Nothing on a page is ever done automatically.
